content.title: Olaparib · adjuvant breast treatment
content.setting: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
content.dose: Usually 300 mg twice daily; follow the individual prescription
content.schedule: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course.
content.administration: Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double it. Check tablet strength after any dose change.
content.duration: For breast indication 00588h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.
content.indication: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.
content.purpose: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.
content.baseline: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start.
content.ongoing: NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change.
content.heart: Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.
content.bone: There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.
content.urgent: Contact the oncology team urgently for fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, new or worsening breathlessness/cough, severe weakness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse require emergency help.
content.special: This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated.
content.contraception: Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss effective contraception before treatment; EMA recommends two reliable complementary methods for women during treatment and for six months afterwards. Men and their partners need contraception during treatment and for three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for one month after the last dose.

logistics.title: After chemotherapy and local treatment
logistics.text: Olaparib follows the chemotherapy and local-treatment plan. In OlympiA, surgery and any indicated radiotherapy were completed before olaparib, with at least a two-week gap after local treatment. NCCP advises starting ideally within twelve weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation; your team sets the start.

logistics.title: Endocrine therapy may overlap
logistics.text: For hormone receptor-positive disease, the prescribed hormone treatment can continue alongside olaparib and often continues after the one-year olaparib course. Its injections, tablets and bone checks keep their own schedule.

logistics.title: A daily routine at home
logistics.text: Choose consistent morning and evening times and check the strength and number of tablets on each new prescription. Keep a sufficient supply before weekends or holidays. No infusion pump or port is needed for olaparib itself.

logistics.title: If treatment is paused
logistics.text: The oncology team decides when and at what dose to restart after blood recovery or symptom improvement. Do not calculate a catch-up dose or restart automatically because a calendar month has passed.

logistics.title: After the planned year
logistics.text: Agree the stop date and ongoing breast follow-up. Endocrine treatment and breast surveillance may continue. Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections, bruising or breathlessness even after olaparib finishes.

support.title: Nausea support matched to oral treatment
support.text: NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high emetic risk. Agree an anti-sickness plan under local policy, and seek review if oral intake falls. The SmPC describes early/intermittent symptoms; do not automatically copy an intravenous chemotherapy antiemetic cycle.

support.title: Check the antiemetic interaction
support.text: Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor in NCCP 00588 and can increase olaparib exposure. The prescriber/pharmacist should choose and reconcile supportive medicines; never add an antiemetic from another regimen without checking.

support.title: Blood and infection support
support.text: Anaemia or other low counts can lead to interruption, dose adjustment, transfusion or additional investigation. There is no universal routine G-CSF course for every person on this regimen.

support.title: Medicines and supplements
support.text: Review all prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs and herbal products. Strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers can change exposure. Avoid grapefruit products and seek advice before starting anything new.

support.title: Stomach symptoms
support.text: NCCP allows consideration of a proton pump inhibitor under local policy. This is symptom- and patient-dependent, rather than a compulsory medication for everyone.

agents.name: Olaparib (Lynparza)
agents.mechanism: Disrupts DNA repair in susceptible cancer cells
visual: DNA damage accumulates in cancer cells
agents.explanation: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.
agents.watch: Keep the four-weekly blood reviews and report persistent nausea, marked fatigue, infections, bleeding or new respiratory symptoms. Severe blood abnormalities need review even if you feel well.
risks: Nausea, vomiting, reduced appetite and indigestion
Low neutrophils or platelets, with infection or bleeding risk
Uncommon but serious pneumonitis or drug-induced liver injury
Rare serious marrow disorders, including MDS/AML
Venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; risk differs by treatment setting
Fetal harm; contraception and breastfeeding restrictions

anatomy: Ask for help early if nausea or vomiting makes it difficult to eat, drink or take tablets.
Anaemia can cause marked tiredness or breathlessness; low white cells and platelets can cause infection or bruising.
A new cough or worsening breathlessness needs prompt assessment; uncommon lung inflammation is important to recognise.
Report jaundice, dark urine or persistent upper abdominal discomfort; liver tests help investigate possible injury.

evidence.title: OlympiA: adjuvant olaparib primary analysis
evidence.population: 1,836 patients with high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer and germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, after chemotherapy and local treatment.
evidence.interpretation: One year of olaparib improved invasive disease-free survival compared with placebo. The trial establishes the adjuvant sequence: local therapy first, then olaparib; endocrine therapy was permitted concurrently.
evidence.limitations: Eligibility was selected by BRCA status and high-risk pathology. Results do not establish benefit for every HER2-negative tumour, a BRCA variant of uncertain significance or concurrent radiation.

evidence.title: OlympiA: four-year survival analysis
evidence.population: The same 1,836-patient randomised population; median follow-up 3.5 years.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Updated invasive disease-free survival; prespecified second interim overall-survival analysis.
evidence.interpretation: Four-year overall survival was 89.8% with olaparib versus 86.4% with placebo; OS hazard ratio0.68 (98.5%CI 0.47–0.97). Four-year invasive disease-free survival was 82.7% versus 75.4%.
evidence.limitations: Absolute survival estimates are time-specific group results, not an individual prognosis; avoid mixing the four-year values with later follow-up.

evidence.title: OlympiA: sustained benefit at six years
evidence.population: Updated follow-up of the same high-risk germline BRCA1/2, HER2-negative trial population.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Updated invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and overall survival.
evidence.interpretation: Six-year invasive disease-free survival was 79.6% versus 70.3%; the publication reports an absolute difference 9.4 percentage points (95%CI 5.1–12.7), HR 0.65 (95%CI 0.53–0.78). Overall-survival HR was 0.72 (95%CI 0.56–0.93).
evidence.limitations: The reported difference uses unrounded survival estimates, so it need not equal subtraction of the rounded percentages. This remains one year of treatment with later follow-up, not six years of olaparib.

clinical_notes: Keep 00588h patient material separate from shared ovarian/prostate/pancreatic durations and consent.

Breast high-risk TNBC after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: residual invasive disease; after adjuvant chemotherapy: node-positive or node-negative tumour≥2 cm. HR-positive/HER2-negative after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: residual disease plus CPS+EG≥3; after adjuvant chemotherapy:≥4 positive nodes.
NCCP ideally starts within 12 weeks after the last surgery/chemotherapy/radiation; this is an ideal target, not a hard exclusion. OlympiA required local therapy at least 2 weeks before enrolment.
Initial blood recovery to CTCAE grade≤1 differs from NCCP continuation ANC≥1/platelets≥100 thresholds.
NCCP/SmPC differ at exact CrCl30, severe renal/dialysis and Child-PughC. Those outputs require source reconciliation without an automatic dose.
Avoid importing an ovarian clinical-trial CT schedule into disease-free adjuvant breast follow-up. No universal olaparib echo/ECG/DXA schedule.
Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor; this matters when designing the oral antiemetic script.
content.radiotherapy_note: Olaparib follows completion of surgery, chemotherapy and any indicated radiotherapy. OlympiA required at least two weeks after completion of local therapy, including radiation, before trial entry. NCCP advises starting ideally within twelve weeks of the last treatment; the team confirms the individual interval. Endocrine therapy may run concurrently where indicated.
